:::{#thm-partial-correlation-precision}
#### The partial correlation from the precision matrix

Let $\vX \sim \Normal_p\paren{\vecf{\mean}, \matr{\covmat}}$ with $p \ge 2$,
let $i \ne j$,
and let $\matr{\Omega} = \precision(\vX)$ be its [precision matrix](#def-precision-matrix).
Then the [partial correlation](#def-partial-correlation) of $X_i$ and $X_j$ given $\vX_{-ij}$ is

$$
\frac{-\matr{\Omega}_{ij}}{\sqrt{\matr{\Omega}_{ii}\matr{\Omega}_{jj}}}.
$$

:::

::: proof

Reordering the elements of $\vX$ reorders the [rows](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix) and [columns](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix) of $\matr{\covmat}$ and of $\matr{\Omega}$ in the same way,
so we may take $X_i$ and $X_j$ to be the last two elements.
Cut $\matr{\covmat}$ into [blocks](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#def-block-matrix) with the first $p - 2$ elements in the first block.
By @thm-precision-matrix-inverse, $\matr{\Omega} = \inv{\matr{\covmat}}$,
and by [the inverse of a positive definite block matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#thm-block-inverse),
the last $2 \times 2$ block of $\matr{\Omega}$ is $\inv{\matr{S}}$,
where $\matr{S}$ is the [Schur complement](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-diagonalization.html#def-schur-complement) of the first block of $\matr{\covmat}$.
By @thm-mvn-conditional,
$\matr{S}$ is the [variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cov-vec-x) of $\tp{(X_i, X_j)}$ given $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$,
so its diagonal elements $v_i$ and $v_j$ are the [conditional variances](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-variance) of $X_i$ and $X_j$,
and its off-diagonal element $c_{ij}$ is their [conditional covariance](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-cov).
Let $d = v_i v_j - c_{ij}^2$, the [determinant](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-determinant) of $\matr{S}$.
The [inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse) of a $2 \times 2$ [matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix) gives

$$
\inv{\matr{S}} = \frac{1}{d}\pmat{v_j & -c_{ij} \\ -c_{ij} & v_i},
$$

so $\matr{\Omega}_{ii} = v_j / d$, $\matr{\Omega}_{jj} = v_i / d$ and $\matr{\Omega}_{ij} = -c_{ij} / d$.
Since $\matr{S}$ [is positive definite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-definite), $d > 0$, so

$$
\ba
\frac{-\matr{\Omega}_{ij}}{\sqrt{\matr{\Omega}_{ii}\matr{\Omega}_{jj}}}
&= \frac{c_{ij} / d}{\sqrt{v_i v_j} / d}
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= \frac{c_{ij}}{\sqrt{v_i v_j}},
&& \text{(cancel } d > 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is the [partial correlation](#def-partial-correlation) of $X_i$ and $X_j$.

:::
